Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-boost-prompt-long-0089", "row_sha256": "a12e6f5c780781b3d71bd815177da81648c418d66a71300937b8343289e4ed1e", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "can you help me put together the family dinner calendar for monday october 12 through sunday october 18? just dinners, please, not breakfast or lunch, and i need a grocery list and a little prep guidance too. this is for me, Daniel, and our kids Nora, who is 12, and Ben, who is 8. Grandma Jo will join us for dinner on friday only. she doesn't need to be counted for any other night. we are trying to make the week feel manageable, not like every dinner is a special project. Daniel said, “we need dinner before practice,” and that is especially true on monday and wednesday.

monday Nora has piano at 6:15, so dinner should be ready by 5:45. a one-pot meal would be helpful because the kitchen is busy when we get home. tuesday is the night i want a vegetarian dinner, with no meat or fish in the meal. could you make enough of that dinner to set aside half for thursday? thursday should be a leftovers dinner using that reserved tuesday portion, rather than a separate full recipe. please keep that connection clear in the calendar and in the prep notes, because otherwise i forget which container is for which night. Ben dislikes mushrooms, so don't include them anywhere in the week's meals.

wednesday is the tricky one because Nora has soccer at 5:30, but the coach may cancel if the field is too wet. we'll know by 2 p.m. if practice is canceled. if Nora's practice is canceled by 2 p.m., plan chicken-and-broccoli stir-fry for dinner that night, and it can be a normal sit-down dinner. otherwise, if practice is not canceled and goes ahead, plan quick bean-and-cheese quesadillas after practice. that branch needs to be something we can get on the table quickly when we get home. use the frozen chicken breasts and frozen broccoli for the stir-fry branch, and if practice goes ahead leave both in the freezer for another week. tortillas, cheddar, black beans, and salsa are already here for the quesadilla branch. please show both options, not just the one you think is more likely, and make it obvious which condition applies to each one.

friday Grandma Jo is coming, and she likes mild food. she told us, “I don't mind trying something new, just not spicy.” avoid shellfish that night, and keep the meal suitable for the four of us plus her. saturday can be a little more relaxed; we have up to an hour to cook and could use something with seasonal produce. sunday dinner needs to be on the table by 6, and we'd like it to be a straightforward end to the week. don't assume Grandma Jo is staying for the weekend, and don't turn this into a meal plan for the whole day.

we are aiming to spend no more than $145 on groceries for this week. that is a ceiling, not a target we have to spend all of. the shopping list should be grouped by store section and give sensible quantities for our household, with pantry items clearly separated from things we need to buy. we already have rice, pasta, canned tomatoes, black beans, chickpeas, broth, oats, flour, olive oil, basic spices, tortillas, cheddar, salsa, frozen chicken breasts, and frozen broccoli. please count those as on hand and don't list them as purchases. the frozen chicken and broccoli should only be used if the cancellation condition for wednesday applies; don't tell us to buy replacements for them if the other branch happens. if either wednesday option calls for another ingredient, check whether it's on the inventory list before putting it on the shopping list.

there is a peanut allergy in the household, so don't use peanuts or peanut products, and please make sure the meal suggestions and shopping list don't call for them. keep the cooking realistic for a family week: monday through friday should take about 35 minutes or less of active cooking, except that the reserved tuesday portion may need enough time to make extra. saturday can use the full hour. please give a short prep note for anything that can be done ahead, but don't suggest cooking the whole week's meals in advance. keep the dishes familiar enough for the kids while giving us a little variety; fish is okay, but shellfish isn't appropriate for friday because Grandma Jo will be there.

could you arrange the answer so it's easy to scan when we're planning the week? start with the dates and household, then use a numbered section for the seven-day dinner calendar. Show the wednesday conditional meals together with their exact if/otherwise conditions, and state clearly that the chicken and broccoli stay frozen if practice goes ahead. After the calendar, include the brief prep notes and then the grocery list with the $145 maximum in view. Make clear that the tuesday meal is vegetarian and that its reserved half is served thursday. Please finish with a practical note that reminds us which wednesday branch uses the freezer ingredients and what we do if practice is not canceled; don't add a conclusion about whether the plan is approved.", "output": "# Family Dinner Calendar Prompt

Create a dinner-only meal calendar for Monday, October 12, through Sunday, October 18, for Daniel, the other adult in the household, and their children Nora (12) and Ben (8). Grandma Jo will join them on Friday only, making five people for that dinner. Do not plan breakfast or lunch, and do not assume Grandma Jo is staying for the weekend. The household wants a manageable week of family dinners rather than a series of special projects. As Daniel put it, “we need dinner before practice.”

## 1. Dinner calendar

Provide a numbered calendar with a dinner for each of the seven dates. Observe these scheduling and meal requirements:

- **Monday:** Nora has piano at 6:15 p.m., so dinner must be ready by 5:45 p.m. Choose a one-pot meal.
- **Tuesday:** Serve a vegetarian dinner with no meat or fish. Make enough to reserve half for Thursday.
- **Wednesday:** Nora has soccer at 5:30 p.m. The coach may cancel if the field is too wet, and the household will know by 2 p.m. Include both conditional options: **if practice is canceled by 2 p.m.,** serve chicken-and-broccoli stir-fry as a normal sit-down dinner; **otherwise, if practice is not canceled and goes ahead,** serve quick bean-and-cheese quesadillas after practice. Make clear that the quesadillas should be quick to get on the table after getting home. Use the frozen chicken breasts and frozen broccoli only for the canceled-practice branch. If practice goes ahead, leave both frozen for another week. Tortillas, cheddar, black beans, and salsa are already on hand for the quesadillas.
- **Thursday:** Serve the half of Tuesday’s vegetarian dinner that was set aside. Do not make Thursday a separate full recipe; make the Tuesday-to-Thursday connection clear.
- **Friday:** Grandma Jo joins the four household members. Choose a mild meal for all five, with no shellfish. Grandma Jo said, “I don't mind trying something new, just not spicy.”
- **Saturday:** A more relaxed dinner is fine; up to an hour of cooking is available, and the meal could use seasonal produce.
- **Sunday:** Serve dinner by 6 p.m. Choose a straightforward end-of-week meal.

Ben dislikes mushrooms, so do not include mushrooms in any meal. Fish is acceptable on other days, but shellfish is not appropriate for Friday.

## 2. Cooking and food constraints

Keep Monday-through-Friday meals to about 35 minutes or less of active cooking. Allow enough time on Tuesday to make the extra portion for Thursday. Saturday may take up to an hour. Include short notes on tasks that can be done ahead, but do not suggest cooking the entire week’s meals in advance. Keep the dishes familiar enough for the children while providing some variety.

There is a peanut allergy in the household. Do not use peanuts or peanut products in meal suggestions or the grocery list.

## 3. Prep notes and grocery list

After the calendar, add brief, practical prep notes. Then provide a grocery list grouped by store section, with sensible quantities for this household. Separate pantry items from items to buy, and keep the total grocery cost at or below the $145 maximum; this is a ceiling, not a spending target.

The household already has rice, pasta, canned tomatoes, black beans, chickpeas, broth, oats, flour, olive oil, basic spices, tortillas, cheddar, salsa, frozen chicken breasts, and frozen broccoli. Treat these as on hand and do not list them as purchases. The frozen chicken and broccoli are for the Wednesday stir-fry only if practice is canceled. If practice goes ahead, leave them frozen for another week and do not suggest buying replacements. Before adding any other ingredient needed for either Wednesday option to the shopping list, check whether it is already on hand.

Make the calendar, prep notes, and shopping list consistent with one another. In particular, show the Tuesday vegetarian dinner’s reserved half as Thursday’s meal, and retain both Wednesday branches with their exact conditions. End with a practical reminder: the canceled-practice branch uses the freezer chicken and broccoli; if practice is not canceled and goes ahead, make the quick quesadillas and leave those freezer ingredients unused."}]
